summary: Zack Beer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. As attested in 2026, he studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

Zalman Movshevich Dymshits (1921–1990) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Moscow State University (c. 1945–1950). He taught at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1953–1954) and became a professor at the Moscow State Institute of International Relations in 1954.

Zarawar Khan is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his MA and PhD in archaeology at the University of Peshawar. He served as an Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).
Zawgyi (1907–1990) studied at the University of Rangoon (c. 1924–1929) under Pe Maung Tin (c. 1925–1929) and later studied at the University of Dublin (c. 1934–1936).

Zayn Kassam works in religious studies and philosophy. She held positions at Pomona College beginning in 1995, served as research fellow (1998) and director (2023) at the Institute of Ismaili Studies, and directed the Pacific Basin Institute.

Zdeněk Materna (1900–1944) was an Indologist who studied at the Charles University Faculty of Arts (c. 1919–1924). He completed his PhD at Charles University (1920–1925) under doctoral supervisor Josef Zubatý.

Zeff Bjerken works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at UC Santa Barbara and the University of Michigan (PhD, 2001) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., he held a post at the College of Charleston in 2001.

Zellig Harris (1909–1992) was a linguist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (c. 1928–1934). He held posts at Penn (c. 1934–1979) and Columbia University (c. 1941–1942), and taught Ernest Bender.

Zeng Yang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yang was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen (attested 2018).
Zenjo Inoue (1911–2006) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji.

Zenkei Blanche Hartman (1926–2016) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies practitioner who studied at the University of California (c. 1943–1947). She studied under teachers including Richard Baker and Mel Weitsman, serving as co-abbess at the San Francisco Zen Center (1996–2002).
Zenkei Shibayama (1894–1974) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who taught Eshin Nishimura. He held academic posts at Otani University and Hanazono University (c. 1954–1974).
Zenno Ikuno (born 1928) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA from the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).

Zenno Ishigami (1929–2020) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at Taisho University. He served as professor and emeritus professor at Taisho, head of Shukutoku University Junior College (2002–2014), and professor at Shukutoku University (2014).

Zennosuke Tsuji (1877–1955) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (c. 1896–1899), he held posts at Tokyo (c. 1911–1938), Rissho University (c. 1938–1948), and University of the Sacred Heart (c. 1948–1955).

Zenryu Tsukamoto (1898–1980) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar educated at Bukkyo, Shukyo, and Kyoto universities. He served at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities (c. 1930–1961) and directed the Kyoto National Museum (1961–1972).

Zensho Kitagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Guohui Shi. He held posts as lecturer (attested 1976) and professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Rissho University, and has been affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Zerkxis Bhandara works in religious studies and Indology. He has been a graduate student (attested 2026) and held a post in Religious Studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara.
Zesho Machida was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as bettō at Minobusan Okunoin Shishinkaku (attested 1990) and was a professor emeritus at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).

Zev Handel is a linguist, Sinologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Harvard College (1988) and UC Berkeley (1992, 1998). He became a professor at the University of Washington around 1999 and taught Zhihua Li.
